title: A project's own handler cannot run a gate tool the way run_gate does: the stdin rule has no name to call
body:
## Problem

`run_gate` runs a gated tool with stdin from `/dev/null` and `DEVBIN_GATE_TTY` set from `stdin_tty_flag` (issue 0088), so a tool that would prompt sees EOF while a person running the gate can still be asked. That rule is written inline in `run_gate` (`lib/runlog:1820-1822`). A project's own handler that runs a gate tool directly -- an override under `bin/.devbin/cmd/<cmd>.d/` -- never passes through `run_gate`, so it gets neither half: a prompting tool blocks at a terminal while an agent reads EOF. A consumer measured four such gates in its own tree and asked for one named function rather than copying the redirect at each tool line. Parked at the 0.1.8 cut; fixed forward in the bundle on hv's word, 2026-10-03.

## Measured at 2ce9411 (0152 v1 on 953d040; cc's evidence pass)

Under a pty, a handler's tool prints `stdin_is_tty=1 DEVBIN_GATE_TTY=unset`; the same tool as a `run:` with `log: true` prints `0 / 1`. A handler reaches lib/runlog only by sourcing it (`bin/.devbin/cmd/test:17-19` does, and `docs/authoring-commands.md:148` documents it); the scaffold sources `helpers` alone (`lib/tmpl/handler:27-29`).

## Fix

`gate_exec <command>...` in the library runs its command with the flag and the redirect together and returns its status, and `run_gate` calls it, so the rule has one definition. It lives where a scaffolded handler can reach it; which file is the review's call. `release`'s child `version set` and its `after:` lines, which inline the redirect inside the release gate, move onto it; the git, gh and CI plumbing that redirects for its own reasons, and `doctor`, which has no gate, stay as they are. The authoring guide and the scaffold say to call it.

## Done when

1. A source-scan arm finds `</dev/null` with `DEVBIN_GATE_TTY` in lib/ only inside `gate_exec`.
2. Under a pty at EOF, a handler calling `gate_exec` on a tool that asks prints flag 1 and reads EOF; red at 2ce9411 (exit 127).
3. The 0088 arms stay green.

## Resolution

Fixed at 44db8915. `gate_exec <command>...`, in lib/helpers where a scaffolded handler reaches it, is the one definition of how a gated tool runs: stdin from /dev/null, and `DEVBIN_GATE_TTY` saying whether a person is there. `run_gate` calls it, and so do the release cut's `version set` and `after:` lines. Inside a gate the flag the gate read is kept for the tools it runs, marked by `DEVBIN_IN_GATE`; bin/devbin drops that mark, so a devbin started inside a gate reads its own stdin, as issue 0088 has every gate do. An empty command is refused. The authoring guide and the handler template say to call it.

Against the done-when list:

1. A source-scan arm finds the stdin redirect with `DEVBIN_GATE_TTY` in lib/ only inside `gate_exec`, a spaced redirect included and comments skipped, and holds the release's two sites to it by name; red on the code beneath this change.
2. Under a pty at EOF, a handler calling `gate_exec` on a tool that asks gets flag 1 and reads EOF: helpers.bats's arm.
3. The 0088 arms stay green, its stale-flag arm among them; a new arm holds that a devbin started inside a gate reads its own stdin, and another, under a pty, that a release's `after:` line keeps the flag the cut's gate saw.

Evidence. 9 mutants, all killed, one of them only where the suite runs inside a gate, as `devbin test` runs it. The arms run green under GNU coreutils, findutils and sed as well as the BSD tools. The full suite on the landing tree: on main 962e0daf with 0157 v2.1, 0158 v2.2 and 0156 v2.1 applied in that order, in a fresh clone: 2159 of 2159 ok, 0 not ok, its .errors empty (seal 20261005-1749), 17:49:31Z to 18:37:10Z; 5 skipped, the same five as cc's.
